name: bot-detector
description: Reddit account signal analysis — three separate scores (automation, agenda, authenticity), shared by the Chrome extension and the optional Node server.
//type: ESM because the Chrome extension is the primary artifact: it must install
load-unpacked with zero setup, so the scoring core lives in extension/lib/
and is loaded directly by an MV3 service worker, which only supports ESM.
The optional Node server imports the very same files, so there is one
implementation of the scoring with no build step, no bundler and no copy.
//dependencies: One, and it is optional at runtime. extension/ and the deterministic scoring
core have NO dependencies and must keep none: they use fetch and node:test
only, per the convention of preferring Node's built-ins to npm packages,
and a dependency there would additionally have to survive being loaded
unbundled by a browser extension. @anthropic-ai/sdk is used by
server/agenda.ts alone and is imported LAZILY, so `npm install` is not
needed to run the extension, the scoring core, the test suite, or the
deterministic half of the server; a backend started without it still serves
verdicts and reports the missing agenda read rather than dying. The
typechecker is fetched by scripts/typecheck.js with npx for the same
//scripts: `test` typechecks and then runs both suites. Both globs are needed: test/
holds the shared core's suite and server/test/ the backend's, and a single
test/*.test.js glob silently skips the server.
`evaluate` reprints EVALUATION.md's headline band table from the profiles
frozen in test/corpus/ and exits non-zero if any of the 81 scores moved. It
reads nothing but JSON -- no network, no node_modules -- so 'the human/bot
separation is not regressed' is a command rather than a hand re-measure.
The measure:* scripts are the hand-run measurements behind EVALUATION.md's
findings. Five of the eight go to the network and none is part of `test`;
docs/evaluating.md says which, and why the ones that fetch cannot read the
frozen corpus instead. test/corpus.test.js holds the no-network ones to
that claim at the import graph.

scripts.test: npm run typecheck && node --test test/*.test.js test/*.test.cjs server/test/*.test.js

//conformance: The per-repo knobs test/conformance.test.cjs reads. srcDirs is the code the
standard is asserted over: extension/ is the product and server/ the
optional backend, and there is no src/ because extension/ must stay
copy-out-able. `server: false` because the server is optional and has no
supervisor to restart -- `npm start` is the only way in.
